title: Cheap & Liquid Options — screen
html:
Goal: tickers where an at-the-money call or put costs little per contract, and the options trade enough that spreads stay tight. Method: price and 20-day realized volatility from Webull (Oct 20 close). Estimated cost of a 30-day at-the-money option ≈ 0.4 × volatility × √(30/365) × price × 100. Real prices are usually higher, because implied volatility tends to exceed realized volatility, especially before earnings. Options volume = 2026 average daily contracts through Aug 28 (Macroption stocks, Macroption ETFs).

For comparison — the core watchlist is expensive per contract

NVDA ≈ $725 · AAPL ≈ $755 · TSLA ≈ $1,373 per at-the-money contract (Oct 20, ApexVol).

Rules of thumb

  • A cheap contract isn't the same as a cheap option. At-the-money options cost roughly the same percentage of the stock price for the same volatility. A $40 contract on a $7 stock is just as "expensive" as a $700 one on a $200 stock. What you gain is smaller position size.
  • Watch the spread as a % of the option price. A $0.05 spread on a $0.40 option is 12.5% lost instantly. Only trade strikes with tight spreads and open interest in the hundreds or more.
  • Low-volatility names (F, XLF, BAC, TLT) need patience, since moves are small. High-volatility names (MARA, RIVN, SOFI) move enough, but they can go to zero just as fast.
